 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. New look, old rival: the Colorado Avalanche debut their Hometown Remix jersey collection as their two game home stand wraps up against the visiting Detroit Red Wings.
 The new threads may be a fresh coat of paint for the Avs, but perhaps revisiting a decades-old rivalry could bring them some new life to go with them.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Colorado Avalanche (9-6-2)
 The Opponent : Detroit Red Wings (7-7-3)
 Time : 7:00 P.M. MST/9:00 P.M. EST
 Watch : ALT, ALT+ (Avalanche Local Broadcast Area), DSN (Detroit Local Broadcast Area), ESPN+, NHL Center Ice (Outside Regional Broadcast Area – US), SN+, NHL Centre Ice (Canadian Broadcast Areas)
 Listen : Altitude Sports Radio KKSE-FM 92.5 FM
 Colorado Avalanche
 The Avalanche are coming off of a 3-2 overtime loss to the Nashville Predators as they head into tonight's contest. Former Avs forward Ross Colton put the Avs down early, but Jaden Schwartz responded to tie things up. After trailing 2-1 to start the second period, Parker Kelly scored to tie things up again. Minutes after overtime began, Devon Toews would be called for a questionable hooking penalty, leading to the eventual game-winner. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped twenty-two of twenty-five shots in the game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Over the course of the week, the Avs been forced to play catch-up to the opposition. While they were able to overcome an early two-goal deficit to Chicago on Monday, they couldn't duplicate the same results against Columbus or Nashville. The entire first line of Artturi Lehkonen, Nathan MacKinnon, and Martin Nečas have not scored a goal since Halloween. Even a slight bump in production from any of these players could have meant the difference in a close game like Thursday's against Nashville.
 In speaking to reporters yesterday, head coach Jared Bednar emphasized the importance of better defensive play over offensive output. "I would give up some [offensive] production over the first sixteen games for a better defensive effort," he said. "That's where I'm at. I think the offense will take care of itself.
 Bednar didn't have much of an update regarding the injured Zachary L'Heureux, other than that it was a long-term injury and there isn't a timeline for his return.
 Blackwood returns to the crease tonight to wrap up the home stand.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MacKinnon still leads all skaters in points (27) and assists (18). Lehkonen leads the team in goals (12).
 The Avs split the season series against Detroit last year, winning by a 5-0 margin on the road on January 31.
 Projected Lineup
 Forwards:
Artturi Lehkonen – Nathan MacKinnon – Martin Nečas
Gabe Landeskog – Brock Nelson – Nicolas Roy
Jaden Schwartz – Nazem Kadri – T.J. Hughes
Parker Kelly – Fedor Svechkov – Logan O'Connor
 Defense:
Cale Makar – Brett Kulak
Devon Toews – Sam Malinski
Noah Juulsen – Brent Burns
 Between the Pipes:
Mackenzie Blackwood
Scott Wedgewood
 Detroit Red Wings
 Even with the moves made in the offseason, Detroit has struggled to find its footing. They sit in last place in the Atlantic Division with a 7-7-3 record and having lost three of their last four games, their most recent coming this past Thursday at the hands of the Vegas Golden Knights at Little Caesars Arena by a 2-1 decision. Neither team scored until Anton Johansson scored early in the third period, but Vegas countered with two goals of their own to secure the win. Tarasov, playing in the place of the injured John Gibson, stopped thirty-one of thirty three shots on goal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Gibson, who sustained a lower body injury during Detroit's 4-2 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning this past Tuesday, returned to practice yesterday. His status is currently unknown. Barring any updates as the day progresses, Tarasov will likely get the start again tonight against Colorado.
 Tonight marks the beginning of a four game road trip for Detroit before hosting Boston at home on November 18.
 DeBrincat and Lucas Raymond lead all Detroit skaters in points (16). Arvidsson leads the team in goals (8), while Raymond and defenseman Moritz Seider lead the team in assists (10). Defenseman Ben Chiarot leads all Detroit skaters in penalty minutes (21), with Kolesar a close second (20).
 Detroit defeated Colorado by a 2-0 decision during their previous visit to Denver on February 02.
